name: UK
title: UK Political Compass Test 2026 | CoreOpinion
desc: Where do you stand in British politics? 70 statements to see your alignment with Labour, the Conservatives, Reform, the Lib Dems, Greens, the SNP and more, plus your framing bias.
keywords: UK political quiz, British political compass test, Labour Conservative quiz 2026, Reform UK test, where do I stand in British politics, political alignment test UK, which party should I vote for UK, party quiz Britain

lab.name: Labour
lab.desc: Your answers most closely match the Labour Party. You tend to support public services, workers rights, and government intervention to reduce inequality.

con.name: Conservative
con.desc: Your answers most closely match the Conservative Party. You tend to favour lower taxes, a smaller state, and traditional institutions.

lib.name: Liberal Democrats
lib.desc: Your answers most closely match the Liberal Democrats. You favour individual freedom, strong public services, and closer ties with Europe.

ref.name: Reform UK
ref.desc: Your answers most closely match Reform UK. You want radical cuts to immigration, NHS reform, and a rejection of the mainstream political consensus.

grn.name: Green Party
grn.desc: Your answers most closely match the Green Party. You prioritise environmental action, wealth redistribution, and systemic economic change.

snp.name: SNP
snp.desc: Your answers most closely match the SNP. You support Scottish independence, centre-left economics, and a closer relationship with Europe.

res.name: Restore Britain
res.desc: Your answers most closely match Restore Britain. You support secure borders, low taxes, small government, national pride, and traditional Christian principles.

bank.q: The NHS should stay publicly funded and free at the point of use; private involvement should be rolled back.
bank.ctx: The NHS is Britain's public health service, free when you use it and funded by taxes. This wants it kept public, with private involvement reduced.

bank.q: The NHS is a bloated monopoly; more private provision and competition would cut the waiting lists that are killing people.
bank.ctx: This argues the NHS is an inefficient monopoly, and that more private provision and competition would cut its long waiting lists.

bank.q: Immigration to Britain is far too high and is changing the country beyond recognition.
bank.ctx: This argues immigration to Britain is far too high and is changing the country too fast — a central concern of the right.

bank.q: Immigrants keep the NHS, care homes, and economy running; Britain needs them, not fewer of them.
bank.ctx: This is the pro-immigration view: that migrants keep the NHS, care sector, and economy running, so Britain needs them.

bank.q: Everyone who crosses the Channel illegally should be detained and deported, with no right to stay.
bank.ctx: This is a hardline stance on the small boats crossing the English Channel: detain and deport everyone who arrives illegally.

bank.q: Desperate people fleeing war are not criminals, and treating asylum seekers as an invasion shames Britain.
bank.ctx: This opposes that stance, arguing people fleeing war are not criminals and that treating asylum seekers as invaders shames Britain.

bank.q: Brexit was a mistake and Britain should move back towards rejoining the EU.
bank.ctx: Brexit was Britain's 2020 departure from the European Union. This calls it a mistake and wants Britain to move back towards rejoining.

bank.q: Brexit restored British self-government and we should never surrender it back to Brussels.
bank.ctx: This defends Brexit as having restored British control over its own laws, and opposes handing that back to Brussels (the EU).

bank.q: The very richest should pay much more; Britain should tax wealth, not just income.
bank.ctx: This supports taxing the very richest much more, including taxing accumulated wealth, not just income.

bank.q: Punishing wealth-creators with ever higher taxes just drives them, and their money, out of Britain.
bank.ctx: This argues high taxes drive wealthy people and their money out of Britain, harming everyone.

bank.q: The benefits bill is out of control and should be capped hard to make work always pay.
bank.ctx: This argues Britain's benefits (welfare) bill is too high and should be capped firmly so that working always pays more than claiming.

bank.q: Britain’s safety net has been cut to the bone; sanctions and caps just push disabled people and children into destitution.
bank.ctx: This argues Britain's safety net has already been cut too far, and that caps and sanctions push disabled people and children into poverty.

bank.q: Britain must hit net zero even if it means higher costs and disruption now.
bank.ctx: 'Net zero' is Britain's legal target to stop adding greenhouse gases by 2050. This backs hitting it even at real short-term cost.

bank.q: Net zero is an unaffordable middle-class vanity project that is wrecking British industry and household budgets.
bank.ctx: This argues net zero is an unaffordable elite project that is damaging British industry and raising household bills.

bank.q: Rail, water, and energy should be taken back into public ownership.
bank.ctx: This supports 'nationalisation' — bringing rail, water, and energy back under public ownership instead of private companies.

bank.q: State-run industries meant strikes, waste, and decline; private companies, properly regulated, run them better.
bank.ctx: This defends private ownership of those industries, arguing that state-run versions meant strikes, waste, and decline.

bank.q: Britain must build far more homes, even on protected green belt land, to fix the housing crisis.
bank.ctx: The 'green belt' is protected countryside around cities. This supports building many more homes even there, to fix the housing shortage.

bank.q: Concreting over the countryside is not the answer; the green belt must be protected from developers.
bank.ctx: This defends the green belt from development, opposing building over the countryside.

bank.q: Sentences are too soft; violent and repeat criminals should spend far longer behind bars.
bank.ctx: This argues criminal sentences are too lenient and that violent and repeat offenders should serve much longer.

bank.q: Locking more people up for longer has never cut crime; prevention and rehabilitation do.
bank.ctx: This argues locking more people up for longer has not cut crime, and that prevention and rehabilitation work better.

bank.q: The authorities covered up the ethnicity of grooming gangs for years out of political correctness, and it must be said openly.
bank.ctx: This refers to organised child sexual abuse ('grooming gangs') in some UK towns, and claims officials hid the offenders' ethnicity out of political correctness.

bank.q: Framing child abuse as a problem of one ethnic group is a racist distortion of a crime found in every community.
bank.ctx: This argues that framing this abuse as one ethnic group's problem is a racist distortion of a crime found across all communities.

bank.q: People should be able to change their legal gender by self-declaration, without medical gatekeeping.
bank.ctx: This supports letting people change their legal gender by simple self-declaration, without needing medical sign-off.

bank.q: A man cannot become a woman by filling in a form; the law must be based on biological sex.
bank.ctx: This is the gender-critical view: that a legal form cannot change biological sex, which the law should be based on.

bank.q: Scotland should become an independent country.
bank.ctx: This supports Scottish independence — Scotland leaving the United Kingdom to become its own country.

bank.q: Scotland is stronger inside the United Kingdom, and the independence question was settled in 2014.
bank.ctx: This opposes independence, arguing Scotland is stronger inside the UK and that the 2014 referendum settled the question.

bank.q: The monarchy should be abolished and replaced with an elected head of state.
bank.ctx: This supports abolishing the monarchy and replacing the King with an elected head of state (a republic).

bank.q: The monarchy gives Britain stability and continuity that no politician could provide, and should be kept.
bank.ctx: This defends the monarchy as a source of stability and continuity that elected politicians cannot provide.

bank.q: Charging VAT on private school fees is fair: elite schooling should not get a tax break.
bank.ctx: This backs the government's policy of charging VAT (a 20% tax) on private school fees, arguing elite schooling shouldn't be tax-exempt.

bank.q: Taxing parents who sacrifice to educate their children just punishes aspiration and floods state schools.
bank.ctx: This opposes the private-school tax, arguing it punishes parents who sacrifice for their children's education and pushes pupils into state schools.

bank.q: Multiculturalism has failed and produced divided communities that share nothing in common.
bank.ctx: This argues multiculturalism has failed, producing separate communities with little in common.

bank.q: Britain’s diversity is one of its greatest strengths, and multicultural cities are proof it works.
bank.ctx: This celebrates Britain's diversity as a strength, pointing to multicultural cities as proof it works.

bank.q: Islam is not compatible with British values.
bank.ctx: This argues Islam clashes with British values. Supporters cite security and integration; critics call it religious prejudice.

bank.q: British Muslims are as much a part of this country as anyone, and their faith deserves equal respect.
bank.ctx: This holds that British Muslims are fully part of the country and their faith deserves equal respect.

bank.q: Some races are simply more intelligent or capable than others.
bank.ctx: This is a statement of racial supremacism — the belief that some races are inherently more intelligent or capable than others. Mainstream science rejects it, and it is historically tied to ideologies like Nazism and systems like apartheid.

bank.q: There is no hierarchy of races; the idea is pseudo-science with a shameful history.
bank.ctx: This is the principle of human equality: that no race is inherently smarter or more capable, and that the idea of a racial hierarchy is discredited pseudo-science with a shameful history.

bank.q: People are being arrested for offensive posts and jokes; free speech in Britain is under real threat.
bank.ctx: This argues free speech in Britain is genuinely threatened, pointing to people being arrested over offensive online posts or jokes.

bank.q: So-called free-speech warriors just want a licence to abuse minorities; hate speech laws protect people.
bank.ctx: This argues the free-speech complaint is really cover for wanting to abuse minorities, and that hate-speech laws protect people.

bank.q: Police waste time policing tweets and pronouns while real crime goes uninvestigated.
bank.ctx: This argues police waste effort on policing online speech and identity issues while failing to investigate real crime.

bank.q: Online abuse and hate crime are real harms, and the police are right to take them seriously.
bank.ctx: This argues online abuse and hate crimes cause real harm and that police are right to take them seriously.

bank.q: Britain should cut the foreign aid budget and spend the money at home.
bank.ctx: Foreign aid is money Britain gives to poorer countries. This wants that budget cut and spent at home instead.

bank.q: Foreign aid saves lives and buys Britain influence; slashing it is both cruel and short-sighted.
bank.ctx: This defends foreign aid as saving lives and giving Britain influence abroad, calling cuts both cruel and short-sighted.

bank.q: Britain should sharply increase defence spending and keep arming Ukraine.
bank.ctx: This supports sharply higher defence spending and continued military support for Ukraine against Russia.

bank.q: Pouring billions into weapons and foreign wars is money that should be fixing Britain at home.
bank.ctx: This argues money spent on weapons and foreign wars would be better used fixing problems within Britain.

bank.q: Drug use should be treated as a health issue, and possession for personal use decriminalised.
bank.ctx: This supports treating drug use as a health issue and decriminalising possession of drugs for personal use.

bank.q: Going soft on drugs floods our streets with addiction and hands the profits to the gangs.
bank.ctx: This opposes softening drug laws, arguing it fuels addiction and hands profits to criminal gangs.

bank.q: Access to abortion is a settled right and should if anything be made easier.
bank.ctx: This treats abortion as a settled right and would if anything make access easier.

bank.q: Abortion ends a human life and the time limits should be tightened, not loosened.
bank.ctx: This argues abortion ends a human life and that the legal time limits should be tightened.

bank.q: Britain should scrap first-past-the-post and elect MPs by proportional representation.
bank.ctx: 'First-past-the-post' is Britain's voting system, where the candidate with the most votes wins each seat. This wants it replaced with proportional representation, which matches seats to overall vote share.

bank.q: First-past-the-post gives Britain strong, stable governments, and we should keep it.
bank.ctx: This defends first-past-the-post, arguing it produces strong, stable single-party governments.

bank.q: Workers need stronger unions and more rights, and the right to strike should be protected.
bank.ctx: This supports stronger trade unions and worker rights, and protecting the right to strike.

bank.q: Union barons hold the country to ransom; strike laws should be tightened, not loosened.
bank.ctx: This argues powerful union leaders hold the country to ransom and that strike laws should be tightened.

bank.q: Terminally ill adults should have the legal right to an assisted death.
bank.ctx: This supports giving terminally ill adults the legal right to an assisted death (medical help to end their life).

bank.q: Legalising assisted dying puts pressure on the vulnerable to die and crosses a line society should not cross.
bank.ctx: This opposes assisted dying, warning it could pressure vulnerable people and crosses a moral line.

bank.q: The minimum wage should rise significantly, even if some businesses say they can’t afford it.
bank.ctx: This supports raising the minimum wage significantly, even against business objections about cost.

bank.q: Forcing wages up faster than productivity just closes small businesses and destroys entry-level jobs.
bank.ctx: This argues pushing wages up faster than productivity closes small businesses and cuts entry-level jobs.

bank.q: Children should be taught to take pride in Britain’s history, not to be ashamed of the Empire.
bank.ctx: This favours teaching children pride in Britain's history, including the Empire, rather than shame about it.

bank.q: A country that hides the crimes of its Empire from schoolchildren is lying to them.
bank.ctx: This supports teaching the crimes of the British Empire honestly, arguing that hiding them misleads schoolchildren.

bank.q: Free trade and open global markets have made Britain richer and should be embraced.
bank.ctx: This supports free trade and open global markets as having made Britain richer.

bank.q: Globalisation gutted Britain’s industrial towns and sold working communities out to cheap foreign labour.
bank.ctx: This argues globalisation destroyed Britain's industrial towns by moving jobs to cheaper labour abroad.

bank.q: Protecting nature and wildlife should take priority over new roads, runways, and development.
bank.ctx: This puts protecting nature and wildlife ahead of new roads, airport runways, and development.

bank.q: Endless environmental objections are strangling the growth and infrastructure Britain badly needs.
bank.ctx: This argues endless environmental objections block the growth and infrastructure Britain needs.

bank.q: Diversity and inclusion schemes in workplaces have gone too far and should be scrapped.
bank.ctx: This argues workplace diversity and inclusion schemes have gone too far and should be scrapped.

bank.q: Diversity schemes exist because discrimination is real, and scrapping them just protects the old boys’ club.
bank.ctx: This defends diversity schemes as a response to real discrimination, arguing scrapping them protects an 'old boys' club'.

bank.q: Energy giants making record profits should face a much bigger windfall tax.
bank.ctx: A 'windfall tax' is an extra tax on unusually large profits. This wants a bigger one on energy companies making record profits.

bank.q: Windfall taxes scare off the investment Britain needs to keep the lights on.
bank.ctx: This argues windfall taxes scare off the investment Britain needs to keep its energy supply going.

bank.q: Long-standing traditions and institutions carry hard-won wisdom and should not be swept away for novelty.
bank.ctx: This is the conservative view of tradition: that long-standing customs and institutions hold accumulated wisdom, so we should be cautious about sweeping them away for something new.

bank.q: Clinging to tradition for its own sake just lets the dead hand of the past block necessary change.
bank.ctx: This is the progressive reply: that clinging to tradition for its own sake lets the past dictate to the present and blocks change that is needed.

bank.q: A good society depends far more on personal responsibility than on government support.
bank.ctx: This reflects a right-leaning value: that a good society rests mainly on individuals taking responsibility for their own lives, rather than leaning on government.

bank.q: Blaming individuals for problems caused by an unequal system is how the comfortable excuse the suffering of others.
bank.ctx: This reflects a left-leaning value: that many problems are caused by unfair systems, so blaming individuals lets the comfortable look past suffering they may benefit from.

heroTitle: Where do you stand in British politics?
heroSub: 70 statements on the issues defining Britain right now: the NHS, immigration, Brexit, tax, crime, and net zero. Every position is asked twice with opposite framing, revealing both your party alignment and your framing bias.

Your answers most closely match the Labour Party. You tend to support public services, workers rights, and government intervention to reduce inequality.

Restore Britain
Your answers most closely match Restore Britain. You support secure borders, low taxes, small government, national pride, and traditional Christian principles.
Green Party
Your answers most closely match the Green Party. You prioritise environmental action, wealth redistribution, and systemic economic change.
SNP
